approach: Add `check_defined_terms(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and run it as one `step!` in `refusing_check`, right after `check_environment_reach` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. It first reduces the request to plain prose. It drops the generated root-cause lines (`Introspection …`, `Cause:`, `Failure class:`, `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:`). It also drops quoted spans (straight and curly double quotes, single quotes that open after a space or bracket and close before a non-letter, backticks) and parenthesised spans that hold a comma or open with e.g., i.e., such as, for example or like. Whitespace-delimited tokens that look like code (`/`, `_`, `::`) are dropped too. It then tokenises with the existing `request_words` and looks for whole words ladder, rung, tier, layer and their `s` plurals. So stepladder and delayer never match, and neither do `ladder.md` or `layer_count`. A term is defined when an assumption starts (trimmed, any case) with `Term <word>:` followed by at least 3 words; it may cite the defining file. A reading with no capability, or with a question, is skipped. The check refuses a reading when a term used in plain prose has no definition. The refusal text names the terms and the `Term ladder: …` repair. The reader is told by a new eighth line in `READING_RULES` (briefs.rs, a brief and not the budgeted reader prompt) and, as for every other check, by the refusal text on the one immediate re-read. The change adds corpus cases and input forms, updates the cited-jobs replay (7bf8 is now caught by the new check, g6vy still by `check_outcome_state`, 0wtc by none), rewrites the `check_outcome_state` doc sentence, and adds a CHANGELOG entry and decision D164. It declares `expected 3% of newly refused readings`, an estimate. The producer loop's replay (`loop_replay`) measures the real share. No record or data file is added under crates/, so `check_record_file` and `AnyRecord` are not touched.

decisions.choice: Match structural words in plain request prose only, using a new `plain_request_prose` pre-pass followed by the existing `request_words` tokenizer and whole-word comparison (term or term+s).
decisions.reason: The previous planning job failed because a matcher over the whole request fired on quoted mentions. `request_words` (reading.rs:3507) splits all text and ignores quoting, so it cannot be used alone. The 7bf8 request quotes 'a ladder of requirements' and also uses the term in plain prose ('Use the ladder'), so quote-stripping must keep the second and drop the first. Whole-word tokens keep stepladder, delayer, `ladder.md` and `layer_count` out.

rejected.option: Run `request_words` over the whole request text
rejected.why: It ignores quoting, so root-cause requests that only quote the words (hestia.rs:466-489 builds `Cause:`, `Failure class:` and `Introspection … prevention it proposed:` lines) would be refused.

rejected.option: Substring match on the four words
rejected.why: It refuses stepladder and delayer, which criterion 3 requires to pass.

rejected.option: Treat every parenthesised span as a non-use
rejected.why: It hides a real use such as '(the ladder)'. Only comma lists and example openers are skipped.

decisions.choice: A term is defined by an assumption that starts `Term <word>:` with at least 3 words after the colon. It may cite the defining file. No criterion naming the term is required.
decisions.reason: This copies the existing `Code survey:` convention (`code_surveys`, reading.rs:3832), which the reader already knows. It is the smallest design and needs no new reading field. Criterion 1's accepted case also carries a behavior criterion naming the ladder, which this design allows but does not require.

rejected.option: Read docs/ontology.toml and treat its terms as defined
rejected.why: Out of scope in the brief.

rejected.option: Require a criterion that names each term as well as the definition
rejected.why: It adds a second condition for little gain. The brief's refusal is about the undefined term.

rejected.option: Accept a definition in the reading summary
rejected.why: The summary is free text with no fixed label, so a check on it would be lexical guessing.

decisions.choice: Place the step after `check_environment_reach` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`.
decisions.reason: Existing tests pin two adjacencies: governance then outcome_state (reading.rs:8374-8377) and outcome_state then environment_reach (reading.rs:8852-8856). The new check reads only the reading and request, so it belongs before the file-comparing checks. `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` anchors on `check_reading_references` and is unaffected.

rejected.why: It breaks the adjacency test for check_environment_reach.
A reading with a missing file would be refused for the file first, and the cheaper request-and-reading check would run last.

decisions.choice: Add an eighth line to `READING_RULES` in briefs.rs, keep it to about 170 characters, and raise the section-size bound in the test.
decisions.reason: The reader is only told about a check by a rule line or its refusal text. The brief rule list is outside the budgeted reader prompt set (the set is CONTRACT, READER_FRAME, defaults and catalog, lib.rs:279-283), so the reader prompt is not touched. The brief lists briefs.rs and the READING_RULES test as deliverables. The line must stay at or under 220 characters (briefs.rs:4409).

rejected.option: Rely on the refusal text only, as check_history_fixture does
rejected.why: The brief asks for the READING_RULES test to be updated for the new check, and a rule line saves a refused first read.
It has 3 tokens of room, and the brief puts prompt changes out of scope.

decisions.choice: Keep the term list at ladder, rung, tier, layer, with plurals. Declare `expected 3% of newly refused readings` as an estimate. The loop replay is the measurement.
decisions.reason: The list is fixed by the brief. The plan cannot see records/, so 3% is the brief's estimate and not a measured figure. `loop_replay` (run/mod.rs:2250) runs the real replay because the change touches crates/, and `replay_problem` (run/producer.rs:49) sends work back above declared+5 = 8%. The declared share is read from the reading's criterion text by `replay_declaration` (reading.rs:4964), which the producer cannot edit. If the measured share is at or under 8% but differs from 3, the producer writes the measured figure into the doc comment, the CHANGELOG and D164.

rejected.option: Declare a higher share without measuring
rejected.why: The declaration is read from the accepted reading and cannot be changed by the producer.

risks.risk: The 3% figure is an estimate and the share of past requests that use layer or tier in plain prose is unknown to the planner (records/ is not in the snapshot). The loop replay could send work back above 8%.
risks.mitigation: The loop replay (`loop_replay`) measures the real share before verification. The producer reads the printed figure. At or under 8%, it writes the measured value into the doc comment, CHANGELOG and D164 if it differs from 3. Over 8%, it narrows false refusals (for example the code-token skip) and reports the rest as an open question to the user. The plan labels 3% an estimate.
